title: Methodist and Catholic attitudes to dancing; grandmother's strictness
summary: Religious views on dances and theaters; the girls were kept to the front steps.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: That's right. My mother, too, didn't believe in people going to any theater or dance when I was a boy, yeah. That's right. I was a Methodist, and that's part of the Methodist position.
You're not allowed to go to dance. You're almost like Catholic, yeah.

Yeah. But Catholic people allow you a lot more privilege. You can play cards, and you can go dancing and everything. Yeah. Because I'd even taught us dancing in school, you know what I mean? The little players, we had to dance, and the sisters were lovely doing it.
I was raised with music and all, but I mean, they didn't believe in the theater or... No one did. ...and dancing, so... I can understand your grandmother would be that way about all...

Oh, she was very strict now. I mean, we couldn't go any further than the front door, sit on the steps. Mm-hmm. The night we had to play, we had to play in the yard. Yeah. With those little, long pants on, those little, long drawers, and she called them made out of yellow cotton sacks. Yeah. Yeah. Well, those were the days, though. Yeah. I'd give anything to call them back. Oh, yes, that's right. Oh, I'd give anything to have my grandmother here. Anything, right. Right. And when my son got married, I was just as blue as I could be. Mm-hmm. My sister left two months before we married, and I mean, I had a lot of cousins and aunties, but I mean, I wanted her.
